_comment: The lifecycle configuration that is live on the backup bucket, kept here so it is reviewable.
The whole reason this exists is that the rule previously lived only as a sentence in a runbook and was never applied for three weeks, which is how /privacy's 90-day sentence came to be untrue.
PutBucketLifecycleConfiguration REPLACES the entire document, so every rule the bucket should have must appear here - including ones this project did not author.
Days must match BACKUP_RETENTION_DAYS (default 90) or the policy says two different things.
Applied 27 Sep 2026 and read back; R2 rejects a rule whose Filter is empty, it needs Filter.Prefix of "".

Rules._comment: R2 puts this on every bucket itself. It aborts stale multipart uploads across the WHOLE bucket - uploads/, papers/, bank_assets/, step-images/ - and has no Expiration, so it deletes no objects. Preserved verbatim: dropping it would silently remove that cleanup for the entire application.
Where dumps will land once BACKUP_S3_ENDPOINT stops carrying the bucket name. Empty today; here so the rule survives that fix with no second round of work.

Where the dumps actually are today, because the endpoint secret carries the bucket name and the extra path segment becomes part of the key. Verified 27 Sep: 27 objects under this prefix, all .dump, nothing else. That check matters because a lifecycle Filter matches a prefix and CANNOT match a suffix - this rule expires everything under the prefix, not just .dump files.
